segments.say: Stop telling AI to make it better.
It has no idea what better means to you. Give it a reader, a limit, and a rule.
Rewrite this for busy readers. Cut thirty percent. Keep every fact. Then list what you cut and why.
segments.text: Rewrite this for busy readers. Cut 30%. Keep every fact. Then list what you cut and why.

segments.say: That last line is the trick. You can check its work instead of trusting it.
segments.text: Here's the shorter version… And here's what I cut, and why:

ChatGPT can lock your chats now. But there's a catch.
Locked chats sit behind a four digit PIN, or Face ID, and leave your normal history and search.
But if you forget the PIN, resetting it permanently deletes every locked chat.
And locking isn't encryption. It hides chats. It doesn't change how they're stored.
Use a PIN you'll remember. Follow for honest AI tips, no hype.
Three AI tools with a free plan, for boring work.
One. Perplexity. Search answers with sources you can click.
Two. Gemini Notebook, formerly Notebook L M. Upload your own docs and ask questions about them.
segments.step: Gemini Notebook: ask questions about your own docs

segments.say: Three. Canva. AI help for slides, posts and simple designs.
segments.step: Canva: AI help for slides, posts and designs

segments.say: Free plans have limits and change, so check before you rely on them. Comment the job you want a free tool for.

Paste your notes or transcript. Then type this.
List every decision, every owner, every deadline. Flag anything that has no owner.

segments.say: The last line is the value. It finds the work nobody picked up.

Your AI might be months behind the news.
Every model is trained up to a cutoff date. Ask about something newer, and it can fill the gap with a confident guess.
Before you trust it on anything recent, ask: what date does your information go up to? Then search the web for anything newer and link your sources.
segments.text: What date does your information go up to? Then search the web for anything newer and link your sources.

segments.say: No web search on? Treat recent facts as unchecked.

Need to say no without sounding rude?
Describe the situation. Then ask this.
Write three replies. Warm, neutral, firm. Under sixty words. No apologies more than once.
segments.text: Write 3 replies: warm, neutral, firm. Under 60 words. No apologies more than once.

segments.say: Three options means you pick the tone, not the AI.
segments.text: Warm: … Neutral: … Firm: …

segments.say: Save this for the next awkward email, and follow for one prompt a day.
An AI browser says it saves your team over a hundred hours a week.
That's the company's own tagline on Product Hunt, not a test result.
AI browsers aim at repeat web tasks. Forms, lookups, copy paste between tabs. What you save depends on how much of your week looks like that.
Before you trust any time saved claim, time one real task by hand, then with the tool. That's your number.
Not sponsored. Comment the tool you want tested next.
AI agrees with you too much.
Make it argue back. Type this.
Here's my plan. Give me the three strongest reasons it fails. Then tell me what I'd need to believe for it to work.
segments.text: Here's my plan. Give me the 3 strongest reasons it fails. Then tell me what I'd need to believe for it to work.

segments.say: You get the objections before your boss or your customers do.
segments.text: Reason 1 it fails: … Reason 2: … Reason 3: …

Long chats make AI worse.
After enough back and forth, a chatbot can lose track of details from the start. Your rules, your tone, which version you agreed on.
The fix takes ten seconds. Ask it to summarize what we've decided so far, as a bullet list. Then paste that into a new chat.
segments.text: Summarize what we've decided so far, as a bullet list.

Sort into must, should, drop. Put the musts into my calendar gaps. Max three big things a day.

People can often tell you used AI.
Out of the box, chatbots write in one safe, average voice. The same openers, the same tidy lists, the same words.
Fix it by giving it you. Paste three things you actually wrote, then ask it to match this voice, and flag any line you wouldn't say.
segments.text: Match this voice for the draft below. Flag any line I wouldn't say.

segments.say: You still read it before you send it.

AI will confidently make things up.
Fake quotes, fake numbers, even fake sources. It's called hallucination, and every chatbot does it sometimes.
Add this line to research prompts. Only use facts you can link to. Say not sure otherwise.
segments.text: Only use facts you can link to. Say 'not sure' otherwise.

segments.say: Then actually click the links. That part is on you.

Is ChatGPT secretly watermarking your essays?
Per OpenAI's October fifth announcement, as reported, it will add an invisible watermark to ChatGPT text in the EU.
The mark is a pattern in word choice. You can't see it. Outside the EU, it's off by default.
There's no public checker. Access is limited to approved researchers.
Check your school's AI policy, and say when you used AI. Follow for honest AI news.
